sections.history: The Araneri Achaleswarar shrine stands within the great Thyagaraja temple complex at Tiruvarur, in the Agni (south-eastern) quarter of the complex, in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Appar (Tirunavukkarasar), counted among the Shiva shrines on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The place is known as Arur Araneri; the stone shrine is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian shrine set within the Tiruvarur temple complex, it enshrines Araneriyappar — Achaleswarar — in its sanctum, with the goddess Vandarkuzhali (Achaleswari) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The sthala vriksham is the pathiri, and the temple tank is the Sangu Theertham. The shrine keeps the form of the older Shiva sannidhis of the great Tiruvarur temple.
sections.legends: The shrine is bound to Naminandi Adigal, one of the sixty-three Nayanmars: when the lamps of the temple went out for lack of oil, he prayed, and by the lord's grace lit them with water drawn from the temple tank — a sign that devotion, not substance, kindles the lamp. Shiva is worshipped here as Araneriyappar, the lord of the righteous path (aram), and as Achaleswarar, the unmoving lord, with Vandarkuzhali beside him.
sections.festivals: The shrine observes Tiruvadhirai in Margazhi (December–January), Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Devotees come to pray for the removal of obstacles in marriage and for the boon of a child.
sections.experience: At the Araneri shrine the pilgrim steps aside from the great halls of Tiruvarur into a quieter sanctum. Before Araneriyappar and Vandarkuzhali, by the Sangu Theertham, the visitor finds the grace of a Tevaram shrine within the temple of Tyagaraja, and the memory of the lamp that devotion lit with water.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: The Araneri shrine is within the Thyagaraja temple complex at the heart of Tiruvarur town, in Tiruvarur district. Tiruvarur is the nearest rail head, well connected by road, with the temple a short walk from the town centre.
